stem: The fi rst Trade Union was founded in India in the year 1918 by
expl: The Labour Union, formed in 1918 A.D. by B.P. Wadia and V. Kalyanasundaram, was the fi rst Modern trade union Organisation of India. It principally comprised textile workers of the Buckingham and Carnatic Mills. Soon after that two unions were formed in Bombay, one in Calcutta (the Indian Seamen’s Union) and four in Madras.

stem: Who of the following founded the Ahmedabad Textile Labour Association?
expl: The Ahmedabad Textile Labour Association was established on February 25, 1920, by Anasuya Sarabhai and Mahatma Gandhi, following Ahmedabad Mill Strike of 1918.

stem: Who among the following had presided over the All India Trade Union Congress held at Nagpur in 1929?
expl: Jawaharlal Nehru presided over the All India Trade Union Congress held at Nagpur in 1929 A.D. The Nagpur session of the All India Trade Union Congress (AITUC) in 1929 A.D. displayed the trial of strength between the leftists and the rightists (or the moderates or reformists). The moderate section under the leadership of N. M. Joshi, V. V. Giri and B. Shiva Rao set up a separate organization and named ‘Indian Trade Union Federation.’

stem: Who was the first Indian to be the member of Communist International?
expl: The Communist International was founded in 1919 A.D. by Vladimir Ilyich Lenin and Russian Party (Bolshevik). M.N. Roy visited Moscow on the invitation of Vladimir Lenin and became a member of Communist International. He was the fi rst Indian to be the member of the Communist International.

stem: In October, 1920, who among the following headed a group of Indians gathered at Tashkent to set up a Communist Party of India?
expl: On 17 October, 1920 A.D. M.N. Roy along with Abani Mukherjee, Mohd. Ali, Mohd. Shafi que, Evelyn Roy Trent, Rosa Fitingov and M.P.T. Acharya founded Indian Communist Party at Tashkent. Hence option (d) would be correct.

stem: Kanpur conspiracy case was against the leaders of :
expl: Kanpur Conspiracy Case was against the Communists who were abhorred by the British Government. Some newly turned communists named M. N. Roy, Muzaffar Ahmed, Shripad Amrit Dange, Shauqat Usmani, Ramcharan Lal Sharma, Singaravelu Chettiar, Ghulam Hussain, Nalini Gupta, Shamuddin Hassan, MRS Velayndhun, Dr. Manilal, Sampurnanand and Satyabhakt were caught by the Government and were tried for conspiring against the Government in 1924. The charge against them was “to deprive the Emperor of his sovereignty over British India, by complete separation of India from imperialistic Britain through a violent revolution.” The Meerut Conspiracy and Peshawar conspiracy cases were also against the leaders of Communist Movement.

stem: Which of the following trials attracted world-wide publicity and drew sympathetic comments from Albert Einstein, H.G. Wells, Harold Laski and Roosevelt in favour of the convicts?
expl: In the Meerut conspiracy case between 1929-33, 32 labour leaders were charged and 31 of them were arrested including the two Britishers. It was discussed all over the world and Prof. Einstein, H.C. Wells, Harold Laski. and Roosevelt severely criticized it.

stem: The Revolutionary phase of the trade union movement in India was :
expl: The revolutionary phase of the Trade Union Movement in India is considered from 1926 to 1939 A.D. M. N. Roy, Muzaffar Ahmed, Shripad Amrit Dange, Shauqat Usmani, etc. were the main leaders during its militant phase.

stem: What is the name of the party founded by Saumyendra Nath Tagore?
expl: Revolutionary Communist Party of India (RCPI) is a political party in India. The party was founded by Saumyandranath Tagore in 1934 A.D., breaking away from the Communist Party of India (CPI).

stem:
Consider the following statements regarding the Workers and Peasants Party:
1. The Workers and Peasants Party was formed in 1927 and was given the form of an all India organization.
2. The aim of this party was to work within the Congress so that it could be made a more revolution inclined party and an organisation of the common people.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
expl: Labour Swaraj Party was formed in Bengal in 1925 A.D. under congress, which was transformed into Workers and Peasants Party of Bengal in 1926 A.D. Thereafter, in 1927 A.D. Workers and Peasants Party of Bombay Province was formed from Congress Labour Party which emerged within Congress in Bombay Province in 1926 AD. After this, Workers and Peasants Party was formed in United Province in 1928 A.D. and in Punjab by name of Kirti Kisan Party. In the conference of these Workers and Peasant parties of different provinces held in Calcutta in December, 1928 A.D., 'All India Workers and Peasant Party' was formed as pan India organisation. Hence statement 1 is incorrect. The purpose of this party was to work within the Congress to make it a more revolutionary party and to organize the general public. Thus, the second statement is correct. Hence, the correct answer is (d).
